concepts.def: Declaration of faith — no god but Allah
Prayer five times a day, facing Mecca
Annual giving of 2.5% of surplus wealth
Fasting during daylight hours in Ramadan
Pilgrimage to Mecca, once if able
Shi'a 20% tax on certain gains (Ten Obligatory Acts)

walkthroughs.body_html:
Shahada — the declaration of faith: 'There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the messenger of Allah.'

Saying this with sincerity makes someone a Muslim.

Salah — prayer five times a day facing Mecca: Fajr (dawn), Zuhr (midday), Asr (afternoon), Maghrib (sunset), Isha (night). Shi'a may combine into three times.

Zakah: giving 2.5% of surplus savings each year to the poor — purifies wealth.

Sawm: fasting from dawn to sunset during Ramadan. No food, drink or smoking. The fast is broken at sunset (iftar).

Children, the sick, the elderly, travellers and pregnant women are exempt. Ramadan teaches self-control and empathy.

Hajj — pilgrimage to Mecca in Dhul-Hijjah, once if able.

Pilgrims wear simple white ihram, circle the Ka'bah seven times (tawaf), and stand at Mount Arafat.

Shi'a Muslims add Ten Obligatory Acts: the Five Pillars (minus Shahada listed separately) plus Khums (20% on certain gains), Jihad, Amr-bil-Maruf, Nahi Anil Munkar, Tawalla, and Tabarra.
